tasks.title: Set up Supabase database schema and seed Amsterdam safety data
tasks.description: Create database tables (lighting_points, incidents, hotspots, safety_grid) and import real Amsterdam open data for street lighting and incidents, plus curated hotspot polygons
tasks.details:
1. Create Supabase migration files for all four tables per PRD schema:
   - `lighting_points`: id (uuid), lat, lng, type, imported_at
   - `incidents`: id (uuid), lat, lng, category, occurred_at, imported_at
   - `hotspots`: id (uuid), kind (enum: park/square/station), name, geometry (jsonb GeoJSON)
   - `safety_grid`: id (uuid), grid_x, grid_y, lat, lng, lighting_score, incident_score, hotspot_penalty, updated_at
2. Write Python data import script in `backend/scripts/import_data.py`:
   - Fetch Amsterdam lighting dataset from maps.amsterdam.nl/lichtpunten/
   - Fetch incidents from onderzoek.amsterdam.nl (Openbare Orde, last 24 months)
   - Manually curate ~10-15 hotspot polygons (Vondelpark, Leidseplein, Centraal Station, etc.)
   - Insert into Supabase using supabase-py client
3. Pre-compute safety_grid (~100m cells covering Amsterdam):
   - Calculate lighting_score per cell (density of nearby lights)
   - Calculate incident_score per cell (inverted density, 0–1)
   - Calculate hotspot_penalty (0.05–0.15 based on polygon overlap)
4. Add RLS policies (read-only for anon key)
5. Document data sources and update timestamps in script
tasks.testStrategy: Run migration and import script; verify row counts match expected (lighting_points >10k, incidents >500, hotspots ~15, safety_grid >5000 for Amsterdam bbox). Query random grid cells and validate scores are 0.0–1.0. Test RLS by attempting write with anon key (should fail).

tasks.title: Implement backend safety scoring engine and route selection
tasks.description: Build core safety scoring algorithm with time-of-day weighting and deterministic route selection from Google Directions alternatives
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/services/safety_scorer.py`:
   - Function `compute_cell_score(grid_cell, departure_time)` using PRD formula:
     cell_score = w_light * lighting_score + w_incident * incident_score + w_traffic * traffic_score(time) - hotspot_penalty_at_time(time)
   - Time-of-day weights per PRD table (06:00-20:00 / 20:00-23:00 / 23:00-06:00)
   - `traffic_score(time, street_type)` heuristic: high for main roads during daytime, low for side streets at night
   - Function `score_route(polyline, departure_time)`: decode polyline, snap to grid cells, compute mean score, scale to 0–10
2. Create `backend/services/route_selector.py`:
   - Function `get_safest_route(start_lat, start_lng, dest_lat, dest_lng, departure_time, mode)`: 
     - Call Google Directions API (cycling or walking, alternatives=true, up to 3 routes)
     - Score each route using safety_scorer
     - Return highest-scoring route with breakdown
3. Add environment vars: `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`
4. Use `polyline` library for decoding; `shapely` for geometry ops
5. Cache grid lookups in-memory for performance
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test scoring with known grid cells and times; verify time-of-day weights apply correctly. Integration test with mock Google Directions responses (3 routes) and verify deterministic selection. Test edge cases: same departure location/destination, routes crossing multiple hotspot types.

tasks.title: Implement Claude AI narration and contextual safety tips
tasks.description: Build AI service to generate plain-language route explanation and 3–5 personalized safety tips using Claude Sonnet 4.6 with prompt caching
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/services/ai_narrator.py`:
   - Initialize Anthropic SDK client with `claude-sonnet-4-6` model
   - System prompt (cached): "You generate concise safety-focused route explanations and tips for women cycling/walking in Amsterdam at night. Input: route summary, safety scores, time, mode, hotspots crossed. Output: 2-3 sentence explanation + 3-5 specific tips."
   - Function `generate_explanation_and_tips(route_data, safety_breakdown, departure_time, mode, hotspots_passed)` → (explanation: str, tips: list[str])
   - Hard timeout: 2s using asyncio.wait_for
   - On error/timeout: return `ai_status: "fallback"` with empty explanation and static tip list
2. Static fallback tips in `backend/config/fallback_tips.py`: 5 generic tips (share location, stay visible, trust instincts, etc.)
3. Environment var: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
4. Enable prompt caching on system prompt per Anthropic SDK docs
5. Log AI latency and error rate for monitoring
tasks.testStrategy: Test with real route data; verify 2s timeout enforced. Test fallback triggers on API error. Verify tips change when: (a) time changes day→night, (b) mode changes cycling→walking, (c) different hotspot types passed. Measure p95 latency <2s with prompt caching.

tasks.title: Build backend API endpoints for routes, safety, and tips
tasks.description: Implement FastAPI endpoints: GET /routes, GET /safety, GET /tips with request validation and error handling
tasks.details:
1. Create Pydantic models in `backend/models/schemas.py`:
   - `RouteRequest`: from (str), to (str), time (datetime, default now()), mode (enum: cycling/walking)
   - `RouteResponse`: route (polyline, distance_m, duration_min, safety_score, safety_breakdown), explanation, tips, ai_status
   - `SafetyRequest`: lat, lng, radius (m), time
   - `SafetyResponse`: safety_score, breakdown
   - `TipsRequest`: time, mode, hotspots (list[str])
   - `TipsResponse`: tips, ai_status
2. Implement routes in `backend/routes/routes.py`:
   - `GET /routes`: geocode addresses (or use lat/lng if provided), call route_selector, call ai_narrator, return RouteResponse
   - `GET /safety`: query grid cells in radius, compute weighted score at given time, return SafetyResponse
   - `GET /tips`: regenerate tips using ai_narrator without re-routing, return TipsResponse
3. Add error handling: 400 for invalid input, 500 for service errors, 504 for AI timeout
4. Register routes in `backend/main.py`
5. Add geocoding via Google Geocoding API or use lat/lng directly
tasks.testStrategy: Test each endpoint with valid and invalid inputs. Verify /routes returns 200 with all fields populated. Test /safety with known grid cell. Test /tips regeneration without changing route. Verify error codes for bad requests and service failures.

tasks.title: Build frontend route input form with Google Maps Autocomplete
tasks.description: Create Next.js page with form for start/destination (Google Places Autocomplete), departure time picker, and mode selector (cycling/walking)
tasks.details:
1. Install `@googlemaps/js-api-loader` for Maps JavaScript API
2. Create `frontend/components/RouteForm.tsx`:
   - Two autocomplete inputs for start/destination using Google Places Autocomplete (restrict to Amsterdam bbox: 52.2–52.5N, 4.7–5.1E)
   - Time picker with default "now" and visual indicator for day/evening/night
   - Mode toggle: cycling (default) / walking
   - Submit button triggers API call to backend `/routes`
3. Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` env var
4. Use React 19 `useActionState` or `useTransition` for form submission
5. Show loading state during API call (disable form, spinner)
6. Handle errors gracefully (API failure, geocoding failure)
7. Update `frontend/app/page.tsx` to render RouteForm
tasks.testStrategy: Test autocomplete suggestions appear for Amsterdam addresses. Verify time picker defaults to current time. Test mode toggle switches between cycling/walking. Test form validation (empty inputs, invalid addresses). Verify loading state appears during submission.

tasks.title: Build frontend route results display with map and safety breakdown
tasks.description: Create results component showing selected route on Google Map, safety score gauge, breakdown bars, AI explanation, and contextual tips
tasks.details:
1. Create `frontend/components/RouteResults.tsx`:
   - Google Map (via `@googlemaps/js-api-loader`) displaying route polyline, start/end markers
   - Safety score: large 0–10 display with color gradient (red <5, yellow 5–7, green 7–10)
   - Safety breakdown: 3 horizontal bars (lighting / incidents / traffic) with labels and scores
   - Hotspots passed: chips/badges for each type (park, square, station)
   - AI explanation: 2-3 sentence text in card
   - Safety tips: numbered list (3-5 items) in card
   - "Open in Google Maps" button: constructs deep link `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={lat,lng}&destination={lat,lng}&travelmode={driving|walking|bicycling}`
   - "Share route" button (P1 — render but disable for MVP)
2. Create `frontend/types/api.ts` for RouteResponse interface
3. Conditional rendering: show AI explanation only if `ai_status === "ok"`, otherwise show "AI unavailable" notice
4. Update page.tsx to render RouteResults when API returns data
tasks.testStrategy: Test with mock RouteResponse data. Verify map renders polyline correctly. Test score color gradient. Verify AI explanation hides when ai_status is "fallback". Test "Open in Google Maps" deep link opens correct route and mode. Verify responsive layout on mobile.

tasks.title: Add time-aware dynamic tip regeneration on time change
tasks.description: Allow user to change departure time on results page and see updated safety score and tips without re-fetching route
tasks.details:
1. Add time picker to RouteResults component (same as RouteForm)
2. On time change:
   - Call backend `GET /tips?time={new_time}&mode={mode}&hotspots={hotspots_passed}` to regenerate tips
   - Optionally re-score the same route by calling a new endpoint `POST /score-route` with polyline + new time (or do this client-side if grid data is static)
3. Update UI: smoothly transition score gauge and tips list
4. Show loading indicator during tip regeneration (spinner on tips card)
5. Debounce time picker changes (500ms) to avoid excessive API calls
tasks.testStrategy: Test changing time from day→evening→night and verify tips change content. Verify safety score updates to reflect new time-of-day weights. Test debounce works (no API call until 500ms after last change). Verify loading states.

tasks.title: Create landing page with grounding stats and NGO attribution
tasks.description: Design and implement landing page highlighting the problem (78% fear stat), solution, and NGO partner *Wij eisen de nacht op*
tasks.details:
1. Update `frontend/app/page.tsx` to show landing page before route form:
   - Hero: "NachtRoute — The safest way home" with tagline
   - Problem statement card: "78% of young women in Amsterdam have been afraid while cycling at night" (cite: Gemeente Amsterdam survey 2025)
   - How it works: 3 steps (Enter route → See safest path → Get safety tips)
   - "Start planning" CTA button → shows route form
   - Footer: NGO attribution ("Built in partnership with *Wij eisen de nacht op*"), data sources (Amsterdam Open Data), disclaimer ("Simulated foot traffic data")
2. Use Tailwind CSS 4 for styling (review `postcss.config.mjs` for v4 syntax)
3. Add favicon and update metadata in layout.tsx (title: "NachtRoute — Safe routes for women in Amsterdam")
4. Optional: add simple animation on scroll (hero fade-in)
tasks.testStrategy: Visual QA on desktop and mobile. Verify stat is accurate (78% per PRD). Test CTA button shows route form. Verify NGO link opens https://wijeisendenachtop.nl. Check metadata renders in browser tab.

tasks.title: Add comprehensive error handling and fallback UI states
tasks.description: Implement user-friendly error messages, empty states, and fallback behaviors for all failure modes (API errors, AI timeout, no routes found, geocoding failures)
tasks.details:
1. Create `frontend/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` using React 19 error boundaries
2. Add error states to RouteForm:
   - Geocoding failure: "Address not found in Amsterdam"
   - API timeout: "Request took too long, please try again"
   - No routes found: "No safe route available for this trip"
   - Network error: "Cannot connect to server"
3. Add fallback UI for RouteResults:
   - If ai_status === "fallback", show notice: "AI explanation unavailable — showing general safety tips"
   - If map fails to load, show static image with route description
4. Backend: ensure all endpoints return consistent error format: `{"error": "message", "code": "ERROR_CODE"}`
5. Add retry logic for transient failures (exponential backoff, max 3 retries)
6. Log errors to console for debugging (avoid exposing API keys)
tasks.testStrategy: Test each error scenario: (a) disconnect backend, verify network error shows; (b) mock AI timeout, verify fallback tips render; (c) enter invalid address, verify geocoding error; (d) test with intentionally bad Google Maps key, verify map fallback. Verify retry logic works for transient failures.

tasks.title: Deploy to production and validate end-to-end demo flow
tasks.description: Deploy frontend to Vercel, backend to Railway, configure production environment variables, and run full demo scenario
tasks.details:
1. Deploy backend to Railway:
   - Set environment variables: SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_KEY, DATABASE_URL, GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
   - Verify start command: `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
   - Run database migration on Railway instance
   - Test `/health` endpoint returns 200
2. Deploy frontend to Vercel:
   - Set environment variables: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (Railway backend URL), NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY
   - Update backend CORS to include Vercel domain
   - Verify build succeeds and site loads
3. End-to-end demo validation:
   - Enter route: Centraal Station → Vondelpark, departure 23:00, cycling
   - Verify route appears on map with safety score 0–10
   - Verify AI explanation renders within 2s p95
   - Verify tips include Vondelpark-specific advice
   - Change time to 14:00, verify score and tips update
   - Test "Open in Google Maps" deep link works on mobile
   - Test walking mode shows different tips
4. Performance check: measure p95 latency for `/routes` endpoint <5s
5. Document production URLs in README
tasks.testStrategy: Run demo scenario 5 times with different start/destination pairs. Verify all features work in production. Test on mobile browser (iOS Safari, Android Chrome). Measure and document p95 latency. Check error logging in Railway/Vercel dashboards.
